name: NanoClaw
summary: A customizable personal assistant running individual agents in isolated containers.

sources.title: NanoCo seed financing and NanoClaw launch history

claims.value: Separate agent containers and reusable agent templates containing instructions, tools, and skills.
Bundled agent-browser skill opens pages, clicks, fills forms, and captures screenshots inside the agent container.
claims.shortValue: Browser automation inside the agent container

claims.value: Recurring tasks with optional script gates.
Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, iMessage, and installable adapters.
MCP tools and a TypeScript channel-adapter interface; public REST API not specified.
claims.shortValue: Tool/adapter interfaces; REST API not specified

claims.value: Claude default; optional Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, or Ollama.
Anthropic-compatible endpoints, optional Codex/OpenCode/Cursor providers, and local Ollama models.
claims.shortValue: Own endpoints; multiple providers; local Ollama

claims.value: Optional Codex provider uses a ChatGPT subscription; optional Cursor provider uses a Cursor account.
claims.shortValue: ChatGPT or Cursor accounts via optional providers

claims.value: Self-hosted Docker on macOS, Linux, or WSL2.
Separate credential gateway, currently OneCLI Agent Vault; injects API credentials outside agent containers.
Admin approval for package installs and MCP additions; the credential gateway can gate credentialed requests.
claims.shortValue: Admin approval for agent changes and credential access

claims.value: Separate per-agent workspace, instructions, and memory.
User-customized code forks; reusable agent templates. Full state export / restore not verified.
Container filesystem isolation and credential gateway.
Open-source software with no software subscription. Supply your own model access and deployment; their costs and limits vary.
claims.shortValue: Free software; model & hosting costs vary

plans.name: Self-hosted
plans.billing: Model access and hosting are supplied separately.
includes: Anthropic-compatible endpoints, optional Codex/OpenCode/Cursor providers, and local Ollama models.
limits: Usage limits and running costs depend on your chosen provider and deployment.

worksWithoutVendor.detail: Open-source software you run yourself, so it keeps running if the project stops; it still depends on whichever model provider you point it at.

remoteDisable.detail: Runs on hardware you control, with no vendor activation or licence check described.

dataAfterExit.detail: State lives on hardware you control, but a documented full export and restore path is not established.
